Dab
DAB
noun / verb (Millennial slang)
A dance move in which a person drops the head into the crook of one bent elbow while extending the other arm upward and outward, like a sneeze. It came from the Atlanta hip-hop scene about 2014 (credited variously to Skippa Da Flippa and to Migos, whose "Look at My Dab" appeared in 2015). Carolina Panthers quarterback Cam Newton’s touchdown dabs in the 2015 NFL season made it a national craze, and by 2016 politicians, grandparents, and schoolchildren were dabbing for the camera. It faded by 2017 as an ironic Millennial gesture. (Unrelated: dab as slang for a cannabis concentrate.)

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To dab is to strike the pose: head ducked into one elbow, other arm flung out. In 2015–2016 it was everywhere: in end zones, classrooms, graduation photos, and campaign events. The Christian observation: a dance move is not a moral question, and the dab was a harmless, silly celebration. Scripture is not against celebration or dancing; Miriam took a timbrel and the women "went out after her with timbrels and with dances" (Exo 15:20), and David danced before the LORD. Two small notes are worth making. First, celebration in Scripture is aimed somewhere, at a victory given by God. The dab as a touchdown gesture often celebrated the self, and sportsmanship includes humility in winning: "Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth" (Pro 27:2). Second, the same three letters carry a darker slang meaning among teenagers: a dab is a highly concentrated form of cannabis, inhaled through a special rig, and "dabbing" in that sense is dangerous. A parent who hears the word should know which one is meant. Paul’s rule fits both: "whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God" (1Co 10:31), and "Be sober, be vigilant" (1Pe 5:8). A father dabs badly at his son’s graduation to make him groan, and also knows enough to ask a careful question if he hears about "dabs" at a party.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial dance move (Atlanta hip-hop c. 2014; Cam Newton, 2015) of ducking the head into an elbow; harmless celebration, best aimed at thanks rather than self (Pro 27:2); note the separate, dangerous cannabis sense of dab.

DAB, n. / v.i. (Millennial slang, c. 2014–2017) A celebratory dance gesture: the head dropped into the crook of a bent arm, the other arm extended. "He dabbed in the end zone."

Separate slang sense: a concentrated cannabis extract; dabbing = inhaling it.

Webster (1828), root dab: DAB, verb transitive 1. To strike gently with the hand; to slap; to box. 2. To strike gently with some soft or moist substance; as, to dab a sore with lint.

Decode for parents: the dance is harmless; the drug sense is not; know which one you are hearing.

Key Scripture

Exo 15:20 — "And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances."

Pro 27:2 — "Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips."

1Co 10:31 — "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God."

1Pe 5:8 — "Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:"

Psa 30:11 — "Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness;"

Modern Corruption

The dab is a harmless dance; its only shadows are self-celebration and a same-spelled slang for concentrated cannabis that parents should recognize.

expand to see more

There is little to correct in the dance itself. The touchdown dab could become a taunt, a celebration of self at an opponent’s expense, and the gesture often said "look at me" more than "thank God." That is a small sin of pride, common to all sports celebrations. The more serious concern is the homonym: dabs of cannabis concentrate are far stronger than ordinary marijuana, and teenagers using the word may not mean the dance.

The redemption is joy with direction and sobriety with knowledge. "Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness" (Psa 30:11). Christians can dance, celebrate, and be silly; let the celebration remember the Giver. And parents should be vigilant, knowing the language of the culture well enough to recognize danger in it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Middle English dabben (to strike gently) → dab → c. 2014 Atlanta hip-hop dance → 2015 Cam Newton → 2016 global craze.

Usage

"Let another man praise thee (Pro 27:2): even in the end zone."

"Be sober, be vigilant (1Pe 5:8): know the other meaning of dab."
